They desperately wanted everyone in America to be forced to buy their product or pay a fine. It was every industries dream situation! What they did not count on however, was how generally unhealthy the US population is, and how big a stick they would need to force people into the system.

Fit, healthy people who don't have employee health insurance are simply paying the "reasonable" fine and opting out, as they don't need the services and are willing to gamble that they stay healthy. Financially secure people are paying the fine and then negotiating directly with the healthcare providers for payment (often saving 40-50% for cash payment).

What they were left with were the overweight, pre-diabetic, unhealhy masses who were either previously uninsurable or unemployed. Dealing with these people's conditions is expensive, not because caring for them is entirely all that pricey, but because the healthcare system itself is designed to inflate expenses and negate liability by over-providing, thanks to how insurance and healthcare providers have collaborated in the past to push the "you need insurance" mandate before it was federally required. The healthcare providers don't really care that the insurance companies now can't handle their end of the bargin.

IMO the best way out of this is to un-mandate insurance at the consumer level, and de-incentivise the "provider-insurer" relationship. First, you remove border restrictions for insurance providers to force nationwide competition. Second, you mandate that care providers publish a legally binding, publicly available, itemized full price list for all services provided. Lastly, you provide a tax credit every year that allows for / covers the cost of 2 preventative care visits annually. Then you wait a couple years to see how the market reshapes itself. At that point maybe you make some restrictions on how providers and insurers collaborate, like requiring providers to list the "lowest price agreed to" for the service instead of a just a base price, or make the tax credit conditional on physician signoff that you've made attempts at improving your health (non-specific)... Rinse and repeat. 4-6 years later you have have well functioning US healthcare system.
